lede: Digits test BPD is 1.210. Fashion test BPD is 3.263. Both inverse-sample grids stay broken.
title: Multi-scale RealNVP
question: Does the coupling flow assign high likelihood to grayscale MNIST and invert into recognizable samples?
process: CouplingLayer splits the channels with a mask. Where the mask is 1 the value is kept. Where it is 0, ScaleTranslate reads only the kept part and predicts a scale and a shift.
forward then applies that affine map, which is the line in CouplingLayer.forward:
The Jacobian of a coupling is triangular, so its log-determinant is the sum of s on the changed coordinates only. That is the next line:
inverse recomputes s and t from the kept part of y and undoes the affine map:

MultiScaleFlow stacks these layers. It squeezes 28×28 into 14×14, couples, and factors half the channels out as z1. It squeezes again to 7×7, couples, and factors z2. The last block emits z3. Each piece is scored under a standard normal.
log_prob is the change-of-variables density. Pixels are dequantized and logit-mapped first, and that Jacobian is added too:
\[ \log p(x) = \log p(z_1)+\log p(z_2)+\log p(z_3) + \log|\det J_{\mathrm{flow}}| + \log|\det J_{\mathrm{logit}}| \]
Training minimises the batch mean of −log p(x). Samples draw the three normals and run flow.inverse, then the inverse logit.

The digits checkpoint is kept in reports/mnist_realnvp/digits/, separate from the Fashion files. The saved digits curve stops near epoch 9, and its test line finishes at the scored test NLL 657.3 (1.210 bits per dimension; train 660.3 and 1.215). Fashion, 20 epochs on the same hyperparameters, has test BPD 3.263. The one-epoch search that chose those hyperparameters had validation BPD 1.583.

opening.summary: Epoch 20 is bold: it is the Fashion checkpoint that was scored. Hover it for the test BPD, then the Optuna bar for the two trials.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Epoch 1 is the first test point on bpd_fashion.png, BPD 3.582. The train curve on that figure starts near 4.11. Most of the drop happens in these early epochs. Intermediate epochs were drawn to the PNG and were not written as a series.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion bits per dimension. The right-hand end is the scored 3.263.

marks.summary: Epoch 20 is bold because it is the scored checkpoint. evaluation_test_fashion.json records test NLL 1773.2 and BPD 3.263 on 10,000 images, the same BPD as the last point of bpd_fashion.png. Train on that split is NLL 1763.6 and BPD 3.245. The loop keeps the last weights, and the curve is flat here rather than rising, so this is the best likelihood the run left on disk. It is a partial success: 3.263 beats an 8-bit uniform code, and the inverse samples are still garment blobs. A tight grayscale flow sits nearer 1 bit per dimension. The digits search, after one epoch, was already at validation BPD 1.583.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion inverse samples from the epoch-20 checkpoint. A few clothes, mostly torn shapes.

marks.label: trial 0 picked
marks.summary: Trial 0 is bold because it minimizes validation NLL. best_params.json stores hidden channels 64, 4 coupling layers, scale 2, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0, batch 128, validation NLL 860.1, validation BPD 1.583. The objective was likelihood after one epoch, two folds, on digits. Generation quality was not in the score. Fashion reused these values.
marks.frameCaption: The digits curve trained from this winning trial. Test ends at the scored 1.21.

marks.label: trial 1 narrow
marks.answers: How could the results be improved?
marks.summary: Trial 1 changed every free knob the other way: hidden channels 32, scale 1, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 1e-6, batch 64. Validation NLL rose to 1050.1 (BPD 1.932). The wider, faster step won. Two trials and one epoch is the whole search that is on disk. The Plotly files optimization_history.html, param_importances.html, parallel_coordinate.html, and parameter_slice.html show this same pair.
marks.frameCaption: Digits negative log-likelihood. The narrow trial was worse, and this is the run that kept the wider one.

charts.title: Inverse samples and both test scores

marks.label: Digits inverse
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: samples.png inverts the digits flow. A few cells suggest a loop or a stem. Most cells are hooks, specks, and broken junctions. The VAE and f-VAE sample grids later in the report still read as digits. This grid does not.
marks.frameCaption: Digits inverse samples. Readable digits sit next to broken hooks.

marks.label: Fashion inverse
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: samples_fashion.png draws the standard normal through the inverse. A few cells suggest a shirt, a trouser leg, a bag, or a boot. Most are smeared gray masses. The Fashion VAE samples keep those garment types readable.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion inverse samples from the epoch-20 checkpoint. A few clothes, mostly torn shapes.

marks.label: Fashion reconstruct
marks.valueText: encode then invert · clothes stay sharp
marks.summary: reconstructions_fashion.png encodes eight Fashion test images and inverts the flow. The boot, the shirt, the trousers, and the plaid stay sharp. The coupling inverse preserves a real image. The soft sample grid is the prior.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion data row and inverse row. The clothes come back.

marks.label: Digits test
marks.summary: The digits model was not overwritten. It lives in reports/mnist_realnvp/digits/, copied from the mnist-realnvp-xyzh checkout, and was scored there. evaluation_test.json in that folder records test NLL 657.3 and BPD 1.210 on 10,000 images. Train is NLL 660.3 and BPD 1.215. That is a much tighter density than Fashion’s 3.263. The inverse samples are still stroke fragments.
marks.frameCaption: Digits inverse samples from the separate checkpoint. Test BPD 1.210.

reflection.worked: Measured: the digits checkpoint, kept in its own folder, scores test BPD 1.210. Fashion test BPD is 3.263 at epoch 20, and encode-and-invert keeps real clothes. The wider Optuna trial beat the narrow one, 860.1 against 1050.1.
reflection.unexpected: Measured: digits test BPD is 1.210 and Fashion test BPD is 3.263. The digits inverse grid mixes readable digits with broken hooks. The Fashion inverse grid mixes a few garments with torn shapes.
reflection.why: Measured: the search is two one-epoch trials, and Fashion reused those digits settings. Guess, not a measurement: bits per dimension can fall by explaining the background while the prior still misses the glyph. A published tight flow sits nearer 1 bit, so 3.263 is only a partial density.
reflection.improve: Keep digits and Fashion in separate folders. reports/mnist_realnvp/digits/ is the digits run. Give Fashion its own search and a longer train. If BPD keeps falling and prior samples stay soft, add capacity in the coupling networks.
